eli5.text: If you run the customer spending report, you'll now see separate totals for new customers versus everyone who was already paying, along with a ranked list of the biggest spenders. The report still looks back at two months of payment history to decide who counts as new versus existing, but only counts each person's spending from the most recent 30 days. This affects whoever checks the internal numbers, giving them a clearer breakdown of where the money comes from.

ai.title: Scale down file tree tokens based on message count
ai.summary: The system prompt generators now accept a `messagesTokens` argument to calculate dynamic token budgets for the file tree. `getSearchSystemPrompt` and `getAgentSystemPrompt` subtract message tokens and a fixed 5k misc buffer from the context limit (64k/200k) to determine the remaining space for file content. This prevents context overflow by scaling down the included file tree when message history grows. The `FILE_TOKEN_BUDGET` constant in `main-prompt.ts` was also reduced from 30k/90k to 25k/80k.

eli5.text: When you have a long back-and-forth chat with the assistant, earlier messages take up space in its working memory. The system now counts that used space and automatically shrinks the file-tree summary it keeps alongside your conversation, so the conversation fits without being cut off. You won't notice a setting change, just that larger chats that previously ran out of memory now keep going without truncating your files from the context. This behavior is live today for all users and applies to every chat regardless of plan or region.

ai.title: GPT-4o and reduced context for file reading checks
ai.summary: File-reading decision logic now uses gpt-4o for non-lite modes, replacing the previous gpt-4o-mini default. The prompt sent to this model was significantly trimmed, removing the system message and project file tree in favor of conversation history and the user request. This change targets speed and accuracy in determining whether new files need to be read. Scope is limited to backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts and common/src/constants.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant now has a sharper, more direct way to decide whether your project's files need to be re-read when you send a message. Instead of checking a long list of system details about your project, it focuses on what you actually asked and the recent back-and-forth you've had, using a faster, more capable model that makes the decision more quickly and accurately. If you looked, you wouldn't see a new button or menu, but your requests may simply move a bit quicker as the assistant skips over files that aren't needed. This makes the experience smoother, especially when you're asking follow-up questions or making small edits.

ai.title: Terminal: Use special prompt ID to detect complete commands
ai.summary: Terminal command detection switched from fragile regex patterns to a unique string identifier `@36261@`. This prevents false positives when command output mimics standard shell prompts. Unix shells now receive `--login` and have `PS1` explicitly set post-RC sourcing. Windows relies on the `PROMPT` environment variable. Changes apply to `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`.

eli5.text: When the app runs a command in a terminal window, it now listens for a special hidden marker (@36261@) to know when the command finished, instead of guessing based on the text of the prompt. This stops the app from mistakenly thinking a command ended early just because its output happened to look like a normal prompt. You would notice this if you run commands whose output includes lines that resemble a shell prompt: the app waits until the real end of the command instead of cutting things short. Unix-based systems now start their shells in login mode with a clean prompt set afterward, while Windows sets the same hidden marker through its own environment variable, and the change is live today.

ai.summary: Tab completion in npm-app/src/cli.ts now auto-completes to the longest common prefix when multiple tokens match the current word. The 'print' command was also added to SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS in common/src/constants.ts.

eli5.text: When you press Tab while typing a command, the assistant now fills in the letters that every possible match shares, so you have less to type. This only happens when more than one command matches what you've started typing; otherwise it behaves as before. If a command called "print" is already handled elsewhere and doesn't need tab completion, that's now noted so it won't interfere. This is live today.

ai.title: Fix terminal first command execution on Windows
ai.summary: Added logic in `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` to trim the prompt identifier from the first line of terminal output when it appears. This fixes an issue where the first command wasn't executing correctly on Windows due to prompt interference. The change applies specifically to the `runTerminalCommand` function's data handling.

eli5.text: When you type a command in the terminal on Windows, the program now better separates your typed command from the system's prompt text, so the very first command you run works correctly instead of getting confused by leftover prompt characters. Before this fix, Windows users could see their first terminal command fail or behave unexpectedly because the system thought part of the prompt was part of the command. This only affects internal builds of the npm-app package; if you're using a published version, you wouldn't notice this change yet since it's still being tested internally.

ai.title: Add description to Stripe meter events for referral credits
ai.summary: Referral credit adjustments now include a description field in the Stripe billing.meterEvents.create payload, removing the previous invoices.update call. This change ensures credit visibility in invoice line items without modifying invoice descriptions during checkout sessions, per updated billing knowledge docs. Scope limited to web/src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts and backend/src/billing/billing.knowledge.md. Meter events with negative values remain the preferred method for usage-based credits over coupons or invoice metadata edits.

eli5.text: When someone earns a referral credit that reduces their bill, the credit now shows up directly on the invoice as a clearly labeled line item, instead of being added behind the scenes after the invoice is already on its way. The change affects anyone who receives a referral credit that lowers what they owe, and you would notice it because the credit amount will appear on your printed invoice with a readable description of what it is for. This is live today for new referral credits going through the Stripe checkout flow.

ai.title: Fix Stripe webhook quota update for downgrades
ai.summary: Stripe webhook `handleSubscriptionChange` now sets `baseQuota` directly from `PLAN_CONFIGS[usageTier].limit` instead of querying `AuthenticatedQuotaManager.getStripeSubscriptionQuota`. This ensures downgrades apply the new plan's quota immediately. Cancellation detection logic updated to use `subscription.canceled_at` timestamp (checking if <= 5 minutes from now) rather than `cancellation_details.reason`, correctly handling scheduled cancellations.

eli5.text: When a subscriber downgrades to a cheaper plan, the system now correctly switches their usage limit to the new plan's amount right away instead of keeping the old one. It also judges cancellations by checking a timestamp (treating anyone canceled or about to cancel within five minutes as canceled) instead of relying on a separate reason field, so scheduled cancellations are handled properly. If you looked, you'd see the plan change take effect immediately for downgrades, and cancellations triggered through the billing system will reflect accurately without leftover access.

ai.title: Fix project root update in terminal cd command
ai.summary: The `runTerminalCommand` function now updates the local `projectRoot` variable when a `cd` command is executed. Previously, `setProjectRoot` was called without updating the local reference, causing subsequent relative path resolutions within the same execution context to use stale root paths. This change ensures `projectRoot` reflects the new directory immediately after the `cd` command is processed. Scope limited to `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`.

eli5.text: You know how when you tell a helper to 'cd into a folder' and then ask it to read a file by its short name, the helper used to look in the wrong place because it still remembered the old folder? Now, after the helper changes folders, it immediately updates its memory of the current folder so that everything it does afterward points to the right place. This only affects internal assistant behavior, not anything you see directly.
